ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, L, N, K are on the same straight line above, and N is between L and K. M is below, MN connects from M to N above, and there is a right-angle mark at N, indicating MN is perpendicular to LK. In the figure, ML and MK form the two slanted-side boundaries of the large triangle LMK, and there is a right-angle mark at M, indicating angle LMK is a right angle. Therefore, triangle LMK is a right triangle with LK as the hypotenuse, and MN is the altitude drawn from the right-angle vertex M to the hypotenuse LK. The figure also draws RP parallel to LK, P on MK, and R on ML, but this information is not needed to find ML. Then reason: Given LN = 16, KN = 9, so LK = LN + KN = 16 + 9 = 25. In a right triangle, the square of a leg equals the hypotenuse multiplied by the projection of that leg on the hypotenuse. The projection of ML on hypotenuse LK is LN, therefore ML^2 = LK · LN = 25 · 16 = 400. So ML = 20.
